chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Hammad from Hariz ibn Abdillah from a man from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

"Whoever enters into the state of Ihram before the Miqat (station) designated by the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and then has intercourse with women or hunts, there is no penalty upon him."

key_terms.أَحْرَمَ: Entered into the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.الْمِيقَاتِ: The designated stations/places where pilgrims enter Ihram
key_terms.فَلاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ: There is no penalty/due upon him

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for entering Ihram before the Miqat and having intercourse or hunting?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the ruling for those who prematurely enter Ihram before the designated Miqat, specifically exempting them from penalties for sexual intercourse or hunting. This ruling highlights the principle that the obligation of fidyah is tied to the validity of the Ihram state itself; since the early entry is not considered a violation of the Miqat boundary, the subsequent acts do not incur the standard expiation. It underscores the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the timing of Ihram entry relative to the Miqat stations.
